records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.L: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me: a message against Mount Seir
decisions.reason: Chapter 35 is a message against Edom. It belongs with chapter 36: the LORD judges the mountain of Seir, which claimed Israel's land, and then promises new life to the mountains of Israel (36:1-15).

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying: (L); The word of the LORD came to me: (B); The LORD gave me this message: (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Jeremiah and Ezekiel. What follows is the LORD's message, which takes no quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

source.text: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם שִׂ֥ים פָּנֶ֖יךָ עַל־הַ֣ר שֵׂעִ֑יר וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Son of man, set your face against [the] mountain of Seir and prophesy against it,

en.L: Son of man, set your face toward the mountain of Seir, and prophesy against it,
en.B: Son of man, turn to face Mount Seir and prophesy against it.
en.R: Son of man, turn toward Mount Seir and prophesy against it.

decisions.choice: the mountain of Seir: Edom
decisions.reason: Seir is the mountain country south and east of the Dead Sea where the Edomites lived, the descendants of Esau, Jacob's brother (Genesis 36:8-9). "Mount Seir" stands for the land and people of Edom (verse 15).

decisions.choice: Edom's hostility: 25:12-14 and Obadiah
decisions.reason: Ezekiel has already spoken against Edom (25:12-14). Obadiah, Jeremiah 49:7-22 and Psalm 137:7 also condemn Edom for joining in or rejoicing at Jerusalem's fall.

decisions.choice: set your face toward (L); turn to face (B); turn toward (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *sim panekha* at 6:2. Literal says "the mountain of Seir"; Balanced and Readable say "Mount Seir". The sentence runs on into verse 3 at Literal.

source.text: וְאָמַ֣רְתָּ לּ֗וֹ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֥י אֵלֶ֖יךָ הַר־שֵׂעִ֑יר וְנָטִ֤יתִי יָדִי֙ עָלֶ֔יךָ וּנְתַתִּ֖יךָ שְׁמָמָ֥ה וּמְשַׁמָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and say to it: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Here I [am] against you, mountain of Seir, and I will stretch out my hand against you and make you a desolation and a waste.

en.L: and say to it, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I [am] against you, mountain of Seir, and I will stretch out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against you, and I will make you a desolation and a waste.
en.B: Say to it, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am against you, Mount Seir. I will raise {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against you and turn you into a desolate waste.
en.R: Tell it, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Mount Seir, I am against you. I will use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power against you and make you an empty ruin.

decisions.choice: I will stretch out my hand against you: I will act against you with power
decisions.reason: The LORD's outstretched hand is his power acting in judgment (6:14; 25:13).

decisions.choice: a desolation and a waste: utter ruin
decisions.reason: The two related words are put together for emphasis (6:14; 33:28-29). The word for "desolation" runs through the chapter (verses 4, 7, 9, 12, 14, 15).

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. Readable says "use my power" for the stretched-out hand (m1).

source.text: עָרֶ֨יךָ֙ חָרְבָּ֣ה אָשִׂ֔ים וְאַתָּ֖ה שְׁמָמָ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֑ה וְיָדַעְתָּ֖ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Your cities a ruin I will make, and you a desolation will be, and you will know that I [am] Yahweh.

en.L: Your cities I will make a ruin, and you will become a desolation; and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I will lay your towns in ruins, and you will be laid waste. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I will destroy your towns, and you will be empty. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: you will know that I am the LORD: the refrain, spoken to a nation
decisions.reason: See 6:7. The refrain is spoken to Edom four times in this chapter (verses 4, 9, 12, 15): the nations too will learn who the LORD is.

decisions.choice: and you will know that I [am] the LORD (L); Then you will know that I am the LORD (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the refrain.

source.text: יַ֗עַן הֱי֤וֹת לְךָ֙ אֵיבַ֣ת עוֹלָ֔ם וַתַּגֵּ֥ר אֶת־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַל־יְדֵי־חָ֑רֶב בְּעֵ֣ת אֵידָ֔ם בְּעֵ֖ת עֲוֺ֥ן קֵֽץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Because there was to you an ancient enmity, and you gave over [the] sons of Israel to [the] power of [the] sword at [the] time of their calamity, at [the] time of [the] iniquity of [the] end,

en.L: Because you had an ancient hostility, and handed over the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel to the power of the sword at the time of their calamity, at the time of the iniquity of the end,
en.B: Because you kept up an age-old hostility and handed the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} over to the sword at the time of their disaster, the time when their punishment reached its end,
en.R: You have always been enemies of Israel. When disaster came on the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, you handed them over to be killed. That was the time of their final punishment.

decisions.choice: an ancient enmity: the long hostility between Edom and Israel
decisions.reason: The hostility went back to Jacob and Esau (Genesis 27:41) and ran through the history of the two peoples (Numbers 20:14-21; 2 Samuel 8:13-14; Amos 1:11). When Jerusalem fell in 586 BC, Edomites seem to have helped the Babylonians and cut off those who fled (Obadiah 10-14; Psalm 137:7).

decisions.choice: you poured out Israel on the hands of the sword: you handed them over to be killed
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "you poured them out on the hands of the sword", that is, gave them over to its power. Jeremiah 18:21 uses the same words.

decisions.choice: the time of the iniquity of the end: the time when their guilt brought its final punishment
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in 21:30 and 21:34. It means the time when Israel's iniquity reached its end in judgment, the fall of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: children (L); Israelites (B, R), with "sons" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The settled wording for "the sons of Israel" in Ezekiel. The sentence runs on into verse 6, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma.

source.text: לָכֵ֣ן חַי־אָ֗נִי נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה כִּֽי־לְדָ֥ם אֶעֶשְׂךָ֖ וְדָ֣ם יִרְדֲּפֶ֑ךָ אִם־לֹ֥א דָ֛ם שָׂנֵ֖אתָ וְדָ֥ם יִרְדֲּפֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: therefore, [as] I live, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, for blood I will make you, and blood will pursue you; since blood you did not hate, blood will pursue you.

en.L: therefore, [as] I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, I will make you [into] blood, and blood will pursue you; since you did not hate blood, blood will pursue you.
en.B: therefore, as surely as I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, I will hand you over to bloodshed, and bloodshed will pursue you. Since you did not hate bloodshed, bloodshed will pursue you.
en.R: So as surely as I live, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, I will let you be killed. Death will chase after you. You did not hate killing, so killing will chase after you.

decisions.choice: blood: bloodshed and death
decisions.reason: The word "blood" is repeated four times. It means bloodshed: Edom shed Israel's blood, and now blood will hunt Edom down. There may be a play on the name Edom and the word *dam*, "blood" (and *'adom*, "red", Genesis 25:30).

decisions.choice: since blood you did not hate: the Hebrew is "if not"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins with "if not", the form of an oath meaning "surely", or it may mean "since". Either way Edom loved violence, and violence will come back on it.

decisions.choice: bloodshed (B); be killed, killing (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "blood"; Balanced says "bloodshed" and Readable "killing", for the sense in m1. The oath follows 16:48.

source.text: וְנָֽתַתִּי֙ אֶת־הַ֣ר שֵׂעִ֔יר לְשִֽׁמְמָ֖ה וּשְׁמָמָ֑ה וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עֹבֵ֥ר וָשָֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make [the] mountain of Seir a desolation and a desolation, and I will cut off from it [the one] passing through and [the one] returning.

en.L: And I will make the mountain of Seir an utter desolation, and I will cut off from it anyone who comes and goes.
en.B: I will make Mount Seir a desolate ruin and cut off from it everyone who comes and goes.
en.R: I will make Mount Seir completely empty. No one will travel through it anymore.

decisions.choice: a desolation and a desolation: complete desolation
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the word for emphasis: the desolation will be complete.

decisions.choice: the one passing through and the one returning: all travelers
decisions.reason: Edom lay on trade routes. No one will pass along them any more (compare Zechariah 7:14).

source.text: וּמִלֵּאתִ֥י אֶת־הָרָ֖יו חֲלָלָ֑יו גִּבְעוֹתֶ֤יךָ וְגֵאוֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ וְכָל־אֲפִיקֶ֔יךָ חַלְלֵי־חֶ֖רֶב יִפְּל֥וּ בָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will fill its mountains with its slain; your hills and your valleys and all your ravines, [those] slain by [the] sword will fall in them.

en.L: And I will fill its mountains with its slain; in your hills and your valleys and all your ravines, those slain by the sword will fall.
en.B: I will fill its mountains with the dead. Those killed by the sword will fall on your hills and in your valleys and all your ravines.
en.R: Dead bodies will cover its mountains. People killed in battle will lie on your hills, in your valleys and in all your ravines.

decisions.choice: its slain ... your hills: Edom spoken of and spoken to
decisions.reason: The verse moves from speaking about Edom ("its mountains") to speaking to it ("your hills"), as Ezekiel often does.

decisions.choice: mountains, hills, valleys and ravines: as in 6:3
decisions.reason: The same four words were used for the land of Israel when it was judged (6:3). Now Edom receives the judgment it rejoiced to see.

source.text: שִֽׁמְמ֤וֹת עוֹלָם֙ אֶתֶּנְךָ֔ וְעָרֶ֖יךָ לֹ֣א תָשֹׁ֑בְנָה וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Desolations forever I will make you, and your cities will not be inhabited; and you will know that I [am] Yahweh.

en.L: Perpetual desolations I will make you, and your cities will not be inhabited; and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I will make you desolate forever, and your towns will not be lived in again. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I will make you empty forever. No one will live in your towns again. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: your cities will not be inhabited: the reading tradition
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew can be read "will not return" (be restored); the scribes' marginal reading gives "will not be inhabited". The meaning is close either way.

decisions.choice: desolations forever: in contrast with Israel's future
decisions.reason: Edom will be desolate for good, while the mountains of Israel will be inhabited again (36:10). Malachi 1:3-4 speaks of Edom's ruin in the same way.

decisions.choice: the refrain as settled
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the refrain.

source.text: יַ֣עַן אֲ֠מָרְךָ אֶת־שְׁנֵ֨י הַגּוֹיִ֜ם וְאֶת־שְׁתֵּ֧י הָאֲרָצ֛וֹת לִ֥י תִהְיֶ֖ינָה וִֽירַשְׁנ֑וּהָ וַֽיהוָ֖ה שָׁ֥ם הָיָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Because you said, The two nations and the two lands will be mine, and we will possess it, though Yahweh was there,

en.L: Because you said, "These two nations and these two lands will be mine, and we will possess them," though {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was there,
en.B: Because you said, "Both nations and both countries will be mine; we will take them over," even though {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was there,
en.R: You said, "Israel and Judah will belong to me. We will take over both countries." But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was there.

decisions.choice: the two nations and the two lands: Israel and Judah
decisions.reason: The two kingdoms, Israel in the north and Judah in the south, were both now emptied by conquest and exile. Edom planned to take their land (36:2, 5).

decisions.choice: though the LORD was there: the land belongs to the LORD
decisions.reason: Edom thought the land was empty for the taking, but the LORD was present in it; it is his land (36:5; Leviticus 25:23). Ezekiel's book ends with the name of the city, "The LORD is there" (48:35).

decisions.choice: Israel and Judah (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the two nations (m1). Edom's words take double quotation marks, as speech quoted inside the LORD's message.

source.text: לָכֵ֣ן חַי־אָ֗נִי נְאֻם֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ וְעָשִׂ֗יתִי כְּאַפְּךָ֙ וּכְקִנְאָ֣תְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתָה מִשִּׂנְאָתֶ֖יךָ בָּ֑ם וְנוֹדַ֥עְתִּי בָ֖ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶשְׁפְּטֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: therefore, [as] I live, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, I will act according to your anger and according to your jealousy that you showed from your hatred against them; and I will make myself known among them when I judge you.

en.L: therefore, [as] I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, I will deal [with you] according to your anger and according to your envy that you showed out of your hatred for them; and I will become known among them when I judge you.
en.B: therefore, as surely as I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, I will treat you with the same anger and envy that you showed in your hatred of them, and when I judge you, I will make {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} known among them.
en.R: So as surely as I live, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, I will treat you the way you treated them. You were angry and jealous, and you hated them. I will show them who I am when I punish you.

decisions.choice: I will act according to your anger and jealousy: the punishment fits the crime
decisions.reason: Edom will be treated as it treated Israel (verse 15; Obadiah 15).

decisions.choice: among them: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the LORD will make himself known "among them", that is, among Israel. The Septuagint reads "among you", among the Edomites. The standard Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: [with you] (L)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words English needs after "deal". The oath follows 16:48.

source.text: וְֽיָדַעְתָּ֮ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָה֒ שָׁמַ֣עְתִּי׀אֶת־כָּל־נָאָֽצוֹתֶ֗יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָמַ֛רְתָּ עַל־הָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֣ר׀שָׁמֵ֑מוּ לָ֥נוּ נִתְּנ֖וּ לְאָכְלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will know that I [am] Yahweh; I have heard all your blasphemies which you said against [the] mountains of Israel, saying, They are desolate; to us they are given for food.

en.L: And you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; I have heard all your contemptuous words that you spoke against the mountains of Israel, saying, "They are desolate; they have been given to us to devour."
en.B: Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I have heard all the insults you spoke against the mountains of Israel when you said, "They lie desolate; they have been handed to us to devour."
en.R: Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I have heard all the terrible things you said about the mountains of Israel. You said, "They are empty. They have been given to us to eat up."

decisions.choice: blasphemies: contemptuous words
decisions.reason: The word means scornful, insulting speech. Words against the LORD's land and people are words against the LORD himself (verse 13).

decisions.choice: given to us for food: ours to devour
decisions.reason: Edom speaks like a wild animal or a plunderer, the picture used in 34:5, 8.

decisions.choice: the refrain as settled
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the refrain. Edom's words take double quotation marks.

source.text: וַתַּגְדִּ֤ילוּ עָלַי֙ בְּפִיכֶ֔ם וְהַעְתַּרְתֶּ֥ם עָלַ֖י דִּבְרֵיכֶ֑ם אֲנִ֖י שָׁמָֽעְתִּי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you magnified yourselves against me with your mouth, and you multiplied against me your words; I have heard.

en.L: And you have boasted against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with your mouth, and you have multiplied your words against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; I have heard [it].
en.B: You boasted against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with your mouths and piled up words against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I heard it all.
en.R: You talked proudly against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you said many things against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I heard it all.

decisions.choice: you magnified yourselves against me with your mouth: you spoke proudly against me
decisions.reason: To make oneself great against someone with the mouth is to boast against them (Obadiah 12; Psalm 35:26).

decisions.choice: you multiplied your words: the verb is unusual
decisions.reason: The verb is a rare form, which the Hebrew may have taken from Aramaic. It means to say much, to pile up words.

decisions.choice: [it] (L)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the object that English needs.

source.text: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה כִּשְׂמֹ֨חַ֙ כָּל־הָאָ֔רֶץ שְׁמָמָ֖ה אֶעֱשֶׂה־לָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: As all the earth rejoices, a desolation I will make you.

en.L: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: When all the earth rejoices, I will make you a desolation.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: While the whole earth rejoices, I will make you desolate.
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: The whole world will be glad when I make you an empty ruin.

decisions.choice: as all the earth rejoices: the sense is uncertain
decisions.reason: The words may mean that Edom will be made desolate while the rest of the earth rejoices, or that the earth will rejoice over Edom's fall. Verse 15 explains it: as Edom rejoiced over Israel, so others will see Edom made desolate. The Septuagint reads differently here.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. Readable follows the second reading in m1; Literal and Balanced keep the ambiguity.

source.text: כְּשִׂמְחָ֨תְךָ֜ לְנַחְלַ֧ת בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עַ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־שָׁמֵ֖מָה כֵּ֣ן אֶעֱשֶׂה־לָּ֑ךְ שְׁמָמָ֨ה תִֽהְיֶ֤ה הַר־שֵׂעִיר֙ וְכָל־אֱד֣וֹם כֻּלָּ֔הּ וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel because it was desolate, so I will do to you; a desolation you will be, mountain of Seir, and all Edom, all of it; and they will know that I [am] Yahweh.

en.L: As you rejoiced at the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it lay desolate, so I will deal with you; you will be a desolation, mountain of Seir, and all Edom, all of it; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Just as you rejoiced when the house of Israel's inheritance became desolate, I will do the same to you. You will be desolate, Mount Seir, you and all Edom, every part of it. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: You were glad when the land that belonged to the people of Israel was ruined. So I will do the same to you. Mount Seir, you will be ruined, and so will all of Edom. Then people will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: as you rejoiced, so I will do to you: Obadiah 15
decisions.reason: Obadiah 12-15 condemns Edom for rejoicing over Judah's ruin, and says, "As you have done, it will be done to you".

decisions.choice: the inheritance of the house of Israel: the land the LORD gave Israel
decisions.reason: The land was Israel's inheritance from the LORD (Numbers 26:52-56). Edom wanted to take it for itself (verse 10).

decisions.choice: you rejoiced: the Hebrew has "your rejoicing"
decisions.reason: The verse begins abruptly in Hebrew, "according to your rejoicing". The Septuagint reads verses 14-15 differently and shorter. The sense of the standard Hebrew text is clear.

decisions.choice: people will know (R)
decisions.reason: The refrain says "they" with no subject named; Readable says "people", meaning all who see it. The other levels keep the settled wording.
